To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the PLS procedure is superior to the PCR procedure, the quality of predictivity depends on the quality of the training set, the relative importance and contribution estimates depend on the quality of both the training and test sets, and that a new methodology is available for determining optimal components for PCR.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following: (a) understanding the quality of the prediction, (b) understanding the relative importance of the descriptors in the model, (c) understanding the contribution of each descriptor to the prediction, (d) determining the number of independent variables, and (e) determining the number or optimal subset of components to use for the regression analysis.
understanding the mechanisms of chemical or biological activity, and with developing the statistical and computational tools needed to do so.
developing the mathematical and computational tools needed for the analysis and interpretation of QSAR data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PCR and PLS have different strengths, and each should be considered for a particular application.
PCR is the best choice for error analysis and for selecting the number of components in PCR.
the use of PCR is preferable for QSAR analyses, and that the use of the optimal subset selection procedure for the number of components is highly recommended.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the PLS methodology is superior for regression in grossly under-determined systems, but the PCR methodology is superior when there are more than 1000 data points and the number of components is less than 20.
the PLS and PCR procedures have similar statistical properties.
PLS and PCR can be used interchangeably for the analysis of grossly underdeterminate systems, and that PLS has a number of advantages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PCR can yield a better error analysis than PLS, but PLS is better than PCR for predicting activity.

the quality of the error analysis for a particular set of structure descriptors is an essential component in determining whether or not that particular set of structure descriptor is important in defining mechanisms driving the chemical and biological activities.
PLS is the method of choice for QSAR studies because it has the most desirable properties in terms of the error analysis.
